The support FAQ, product guide, and customer interviews collectively describe scanned PDF handling as a major challenge requiring OCR, with specific technical, operational, and quality implications:

- **OCR is mandatory for scanned PDFs.** Support FAQ states scanned PDFs require OCR processing; without OCR they cannot be searched and citations cannot be generated [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. The product guide confirms that scanned or image-only PDFs require OCR processing [NL-002#NL-002-S08].
- **Standard parser fails on image-only PDFs.** The FAQ notes KnowledgeHub's standard parser only reads digital text layers, so scanned uploads yield zero text without OCR [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. A customer interview concurs that the standard parser can only index an image-only scan as a single metadata block rather than granular text chunks [NL-024#NL-024-S04].
- **OCR output is heuristic and can introduce errors.** The FAQ warns of misread characters, broken paragraphs, garbled tables, and ignored handwriting due to OCR limitations [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. A clinical customer reports missed safety-critical steps (e.g., ventilator alarm settings) because text extraction failed on a scanned page [NL-018#NL-018-S05].
- **Citation quality suffers directly from scanned PDF issues.** The FAQ lists broken citations, knowledge gaps, and longer processing times as consequences of OCR failure [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. Customer interviews quantify this: BrightPath sees about 45% of its corpus as scanned PDFs, leading to missing citations or citations pointing to page 1 of a 150-page document [NL-024#NL-024-S04]; support tickets show ingestion/OCR issues are the largest category (112 of 412 tickets, ~27%) with scanned PDFs making up 40–50% of legacy files for regulated customers [NL-021#NL-021-S02].
- **Recommended remediation includes source cleanup and advanced OCR.** FAQ advises exporting native text-searchable PDFs, converting tables to CSV/XLSX, and using the Advanced OCR Pipeline (Enterprise add-on) [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. Customer interviews echo this: NovaLearn recommends uploading native DOCX/text files or excluding scans until the Advanced OCR Pipeline releases (targeted August 2026) [NL-024#NL-024-S04, NL-018#NL-018-S05, NL-017#NL-017-S06].
- **Manual pre-processing is a heavy burden.** Customers report having to manually run OCR on their own before upload, which delays onboarding and consumes IT resources [NL-018#NL-018-S05, NL-017#NL-017-S06].
- **Future pipeline will require validation and careful queue design.** One customer demands a preview interface with side-by-side image/text review to catch OCR misreads, such as “0.5 mg” becoming “5 mg” [NL-018#NL-018-S05]. Engineering discussions address queue architecture (split fast vs. batch/OCR queues, rate limits, page caps per plan) to avoid blocking normal uploads and memory issues [NL-021#NL-021-S06].

Collectively, these sources agree that scanned PDFs are unsupported for reliable text extraction and citation without OCR, that current OCR is imperfect and can cause serious accuracy and trust issues, and that the planned Advanced OCR pipeline (August 2026) plus source-quality improvements are the primary paths forward.
